added_models.model: Ex-vivo single-cell buoyant-mass response (suspended microchannel resonator) of primary MCL cells to acalabrutinib

efficacy.population: MCL, relapsed/refractory and untreated (AVO trial, NCT04855695)
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC12680032). Opening entry at the method's first MCL use (bioRxiv May 2025).
efficacy.note: Ex-vivo acalabrutinib-induced mass change in pretreatment MCL cells proposed as a per-patient sensitivity readout.
efficacy.short: Ex-vivo mass response as BTKi readout
efficacy.quote: In addition, changes in cell buoyant mass within primary patient specimens ex vivo correlate with sensitivity to Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors in vivo in MCL and chronic lymphocytic leukemia, another B cell malignancy.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry; the comparison is in the same paper.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: ex-vivo mass response (P<0.05) vs circulating-lymphocyte kinetics on 4 weeks of acalabrutinib
efficacy.population: MCL, relapsed/refractory and untreated (AVO trial, NCT04855695)
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. Four MCL patients (two more, two less sensitive), sensitivity defined by WBC kinetics, not the trial's primary endpoint; three of four untreated, outside the R/R population. One pirtobrutinib case is outside the member list.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: pre- and post-treatment samples were assayed together after the cycle-1 lymphocyte response was known, so retro, not same. Patient-level: it asks which patient responds.
efficacy.note: Pretreatment cells from the two acalabrutinib-sensitive patients lost mass ex vivo; the two less-sensitive patients' cells did not.
efficacy.quote: In addition, changes in cell buoyant mass within primary patient specimens ex vivo correlate with sensitivity to Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors in vivo in MCL and chronic lymphocytic leukemia, another B cell malignancy.

added_models.model: MCL cell-line pharmacogenomic panel (classical vs alternative NF-kB; TRAF2/BIRC3 lesions predict ibrutinib insensitivity)

efficacy.population: MCL with TRAF2/BIRC3 lesions (15% of 165 patients)
efficacy.note: Cell lines with alternative NF-kB (TRAF2/BIRC3) lesions were ibrutinib-insensitive; predicts primary resistance in lesion-bearing patients.
efficacy.quote: Although they are associated with insensitivity to ibrutinib, lesions in the alternative NF-κB pathway conferred dependence on the protein kinase NIK (also called mitogen-activated protein 3 kinase 14 or MAP3K14) both in vitro and in vivo.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the epub (2013-12-22); no ibrutinib patient genotype-response data then.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: BIRC3-altered vs wild-type outcome in the RAY trial
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). The BIRC3 effect is reported for the RAY cohort, not shown separately for the ibrutinib arm, so it may be prognostic rather than ibrutinib-specific.
efficacy.judgement: Paired comparison: Rahal's cell-line prediction against BIRC3 outcomes in the phase 3 RAY trial (PFS primary). Direction agrees; partial because not ibrutinib-arm-specific. Jain 2021 (first-line, with rituximab) is supporting only.
efficacy.note: In RAY (ibrutinib vs temsirolimus, R/R MCL), BIRC3 mutations/deletions carried worse outcomes, as the cell lines predicted.
efficacy.short: BIRC3 lesions did worse in RAY
efficacy.quote: We showed the negative impact of BIRC3 mutations/deletions on outcomes in this cohort and identified that deletion of chromosome 8p23.3 also negatively impacts survival.

patient_trials.quote: Differential overexpression of CCND1, BIRC3, BANK1, SETBP1, AXIN2, and IL2RA was noted in partial responders compared with patients with complete response.

added_models.model: Zanubrutinib GLP toxicology and safety pharmacology (rat, dog)

safety.confidence_note: Proxy year: first-in-human BGB-3111-AU-003 started 2014-09-04; toxicology data unpublished until the 2019 review.
safety.note: Rat (26-week) and dog (39-week) toxicology and dog telemetry supported first-in-human dosing of zanubrutinib.
safety.quote: Zanubrutinib was administered once daily to rats and dogs in studies up to 6 months in rats and 9 months in dogs.

safety.confidence_note: Bundled review text (Reference ID 4519846). The review lists animal multi-organ hemorrhage, which matched patient bleeding (~50%, major 3%); dogs showed raised platelets.
safety.judgement: Judgement call, as on the ibrutinib track: hemorrhage was predicted and held, but dog telemetry was silent on atrial fibrillation/flutter (2% of patients) and platelets rose in dogs while patients had thrombocytopenia; a miss on a harm dogs can show outweighs the matched bleeding.
safety.note: Animals showed hemorrhage, matching patient bleeding, but dog telemetry showed no cardiac effect; patients had atrial fibrillation/flutter and thrombocytopenia.
safety.quote: Zanubrutinib had no toxicologically-significant effects on cardiovascular function in a cardiovascular study in telemetered dogs, and had no effects on neurobehavioral function, temperature, or respiratory function in CNS and respiratory studies conducted in male rats.

considered_not_added: Acalabrutinib rat/dog toxicology (NDA 210259 review): rat heart hemorrhage/necrosis only at lethal doses, dog red-cell decreases; dog telemetry result and platelet findings not verified within budget, so no status call made
Acalabrutinib canine B-NHL (Harrington 2016) and zanubrutinib PBMC/lymph-node occupancy (Tam 2019): same systems as the draft's canine-spontaneous-bnhl and btk-probe-occupancy tracks, no new track
